lessons.title: You can lose all of it.
lessons.body: Projects can fail. A storm, a slow season, or a mistake can use up the money. You may get none of it back.
lessons.rule: Only put in money you can afford to lose.
lessons.action: Decide the most you can lose before you choose an amount.

lessons.title: You cannot easily sell units.
lessons.body: There is no market for them yet. You should plan to leave the money in. Do not count on selling when you want cash.
lessons.rule: Plan to leave the money in.
lessons.action: Only commit money you can leave in.

lessons.title: It can take years, and it may pay nothing.
lessons.body: Small projects grow slowly. There is no date when money comes back. It may never pay.
lessons.rule: Do not commit because you hope it pays soon.
lessons.action: Read this again if you want the money back soon.

lessons.title: Prices move.
lessons.body: Bitcoin and the local currency can both rise or fall against your own money. The same project can feel bigger or smaller later.
lessons.rule: What you put in can be worth more or less later.
lessons.action: Think about the money in your own currency.

lessons.title: Spread it out.
lessons.body: Several smaller amounts in different projects are safer than one large one. If one project fails, the others can still go on.
lessons.rule: Do not put all your money in one project.
lessons.action: Look at more than one project before you commit.

lessons.title: Keep the money apart.
lessons.body: Business money and home money get mixed up easily. When they mix, you cannot tell if the project is working. Use one pot for the project and another pot for home.
lessons.rule: Keep business money separate from home money.
lessons.action: Put this week's project money in its own pot.

lessons.title: Pay yourself the same amount.
lessons.body: If you take a different amount every week, the project looks better or worse than it is. Pick one amount and take only that.
lessons.rule: Pay yourself a fixed amount each week.
lessons.action: Choose the amount you will pay yourself this week.

lessons.title: Write it down every day.
lessons.body: Cash you do not write down is easy to forget. At the end of the day, write what came in and what went out.
lessons.rule: Write down cash in and cash out every day.
lessons.action: Write down today's cash in and cash out.

lessons.title: Count the cash.
lessons.body: Count the project cash at the same time each week. If it grew, the week went well. If it shrank, look at what went out.
lessons.rule: Count your cash at the same time each week. The change is roughly your profit.
lessons.action: Pick the day you will count the cash.

lessons.title: Keep some back.
lessons.body: Some weeks are quiet. Things break. If you spend everything, a slow week can stop the work.
lessons.rule: Keep some back for slow weeks and repairs.
lessons.action: Leave some project money untouched this week.

lessons.title: See what nearby places charge.
lessons.body: Guests compare you with the place down the road. Ask what those places charge for a night. Then choose what you will ask.
lessons.rule: Check what nearby places charge before you set yours.
lessons.action: Ask two nearby places what they charge.

lessons.title: Ask every guest.
lessons.body: A guest who leaves quietly may not come back. Ask before they go. Write down what they say.
lessons.rule: Ask every guest what went well and what did not.
lessons.action: Ask the next guest what went well.

lessons.title: Check the place each week.
lessons.body: Small breaks get big if you wait. Once a week, walk every room. Write down what to fix.
lessons.rule: Walk the whole place once a week and note what needs work.
lessons.action: Walk the place and write one thing to fix.

lessons.title: Use a slow week.
lessons.body: Quiet weeks feel hard, but they are useful. Use one to repair or clean. Do not spend the reserve just to feel busy.
lessons.rule: In a slow week, fix something you have been putting off.
lessons.action: Pick one repair to do if this week is quiet.

lessons.title: Read the reviews.
lessons.body: Reviews tell the next guest what to expect. Read them. Thank people. Fix what they name if you can.
lessons.rule: Read new reviews and reply to each one.
lessons.action: Read the newest review and reply.

lessons.title: Keep one cleaning standard.
lessons.body: Guests notice a dirty corner. Write down what clean means for a room. Check each room against that list.
lessons.rule: Every room should meet the same cleaning standard.
lessons.action: Write the cleaning list for one room.

lessons.title: See what nearby farms charge.
lessons.body: Buyers know what other farms ask. Ask what farms nearby got for the same food. Then choose what you will ask.
lessons.rule: Check what nearby farms charge before you set yours.
lessons.action: Ask two nearby farms what they got for this food.

lessons.title: Ask every buyer.
lessons.body: A buyer can tell you what sold and what sat. Ask each one. Write down what they say.
lessons.rule: Ask every buyer what they want next time.
lessons.action: Ask the next buyer what they want next time.

lessons.title: Walk the plot each week.
lessons.body: Pests, leaks, and broken fences start small. Walk the plot on the same day each week. Write down what to fix.
lessons.rule: Walk the plot once a week and note what needs work.
lessons.action: Walk the plot and write one thing to fix.

lessons.title: Use a slow week.
lessons.body: When sales are quiet, the work does not stop. Mend tools and clear a bed. Check that the store is ready.
lessons.rule: In a slow week, mend tools and get ready for the next one.
lessons.action: Pick one tool or bed to mend if this week is quiet.

lessons.title: Store it so it keeps.
lessons.body: Food that gets wet or hot can spoil. Check the store. Cover what is open. Move what is too warm.
lessons.rule: Keep stored food dry, cool, and covered.
lessons.action: Check the store and cover anything open.

lessons.title: Sell it before it spoils.
lessons.body: Some food cannot wait. If it will spoil, sell it or use it. Do not let it sit until it is waste.
lessons.rule: Sell food that will not keep before it spoils.
lessons.action: Find the food that will spoil first and plan to sell it.

lessons.title: See what others charge.
lessons.body: People compare your work with the last person they paid. Ask what others charge for the same help. Then choose what you will ask.
lessons.rule: Check what nearby people charge before you set yours.
lessons.action: Ask two nearby people what they charge for this work.

lessons.title: Ask every customer.
lessons.body: The person who paid can tell you if the power stayed on. Ask them. Write down what they say.
lessons.rule: Ask every customer what went well and what did not.
lessons.action: Ask the next customer what went well.

lessons.title: Look over the gear each week.
lessons.body: Dust and loose parts show up on a weekly look. Look, and write down what you see. Do not take gear apart if you were not trained.
lessons.rule: Look over the gear once a week and note what needs work.
lessons.action: Look over the gear and write one thing to fix.

lessons.title: Use a slow week.
lessons.body: A quiet week is a good time to label parts and clean tools. Keep some money back for a later repair.
lessons.rule: In a slow week, tidy the tools and check the spare parts.
lessons.action: Tidy the tools if this week is quiet.

lessons.title: See what others charge.
lessons.body: People know what a pump repair or a tank setup cost last time. Ask what others charge. Then choose what you will ask.
lessons.rule: Check what nearby people charge before you set yours.
lessons.action: Ask two nearby people what they charge for this work.

lessons.title: Ask every customer.
lessons.body: Ask if the water is reaching them and what is still hard. Write down what they say.
lessons.rule: Ask every customer what went well and what did not.
lessons.action: Ask the next customer what is still hard.

lessons.title: Check the water each week.
lessons.body: Look at the tank, the cover, and the pipes. Write down leaks. Do not drink from a tank that is not finished.
lessons.rule: Check the tank and pipes once a week.
lessons.action: Check the cover and write one thing to fix.

lessons.title: Use a slow week.
lessons.body: When few people call, clear around the tank and check the cover. A clear path makes the next repair safer.
lessons.rule: In a slow week, clear the tank area and check the cover.
lessons.action: Clear around the tank if this week is quiet.

lessons.title: See what others charge.
lessons.body: People compare a hub or a link with the last one they paid for. Ask what others charge. Then choose what you will ask.
lessons.rule: Check what nearby people charge before you set yours.
lessons.action: Ask two nearby people what they charge for this work.

lessons.title: Ask every customer.
lessons.body: Ask if the link stayed up and what was hard to use. Write down what they say.
lessons.rule: Ask every customer what went well and what did not.
lessons.action: Ask the next customer if the link stayed up.

lessons.title: Check the hub each week.
lessons.body: Look at the hub once a week. Note loose cables. Do not climb in the rain or in strong wind.
lessons.rule: Check the hub once a week and note what needs work.
lessons.action: Look at the hub and write one thing to fix.

lessons.title: Use a slow week.
lessons.body: A quiet week is a good time to label cables and see that the hub still comes on. Stay on the ground if the weather is bad.
lessons.rule: In a slow week, label cables and check that the hub comes on.
lessons.action: Label one cable if this week is quiet.

lessons.title: See what nearby classes ask.
lessons.body: Families compare your class with others nearby. Ask what those classes ask families to pay. Then choose what you will ask.
lessons.rule: Check what nearby classes charge before you set yours.
lessons.action: Ask two nearby classes what families pay.

lessons.title: Ask every family.
lessons.body: A family can tell you what helped and what was confusing. Ask them. Write down what they say.
lessons.rule: Ask every family what went well and what did not.
lessons.action: Ask the next family what was confusing.

lessons.title: Check the room each week.
lessons.body: Walk the room once a week. Look at benches, books, and the way out. Write down what to fix.
lessons.rule: Walk the room once a week and note what needs work.
lessons.action: Walk the room and write one thing to fix.

lessons.title: Use a slow week.
lessons.body: When the room is quiet, fix a bench or sort the books. A tidy room is easier to teach in.
lessons.rule: In a slow week, fix one thing in the room.
lessons.action: Sort the books or fix a bench if this week is quiet.

lessons.title: See what nearby rooms charge.
lessons.body: People compare your room with the last place they visited. Ask what those places charge. Then choose what you will ask.
lessons.rule: Check what nearby rooms charge before you set yours.
lessons.action: Ask two nearby rooms what they charge.

lessons.title: Ask every person.
lessons.body: Ask what was clear and what was not. Write it down. Do not give medicine unless you are trained to do that.
lessons.rule: Ask every person what was clear and what was not.
lessons.action: Ask the next person what was not clear.

lessons.title: Check the room each week.
lessons.body: Walk the room and look at the cold box. The door should shut. Write down what to fix. Call a trained person when someone is ill.
lessons.rule: Check the room and the cold box once a week.
lessons.action: Check that the cold box door shuts.

lessons.title: Use a slow week.
lessons.body: When the room is quiet, clean it and check the cold box. Do not throw out medicine. Ask a trained person first.
lessons.rule: In a slow week, clean the room and check the cold box.
lessons.action: Clean the room if this week is quiet.

lessons.title: Stay safe while you build.
lessons.body: Wear shoes that cover your feet. Keep the floor clear so no one trips. Stop and tell the organizer if something feels unsafe.
lessons.rule: A clear floor and covered feet prevent most falls.
lessons.action: Clear the floor before you start today.

lessons.title: Stay safe in the rooms.
lessons.body: Keep floors dry so no one slips. Bend your knees when you lift. Ask for help with anything heavy.
lessons.rule: Dry floors and shared lifts keep people safe.
lessons.action: Wipe wet floors before guests walk there.

lessons.title: Stay safe on the plot.
lessons.body: Wear shoes and a hat. Wash your hands before you eat. Stop if you feel dizzy in the heat and drink water.
lessons.rule: Cover your feet, wash your hands, and rest in the heat.
lessons.action: Wash your hands before you eat today.

lessons.title: Stay safe in the kitchen.
lessons.body: Wash your hands. Keep raw food away from cooked food. Turn pots off when you step away.
lessons.rule: Clean hands and a turned-off pot prevent most kitchen harm.
lessons.action: Wash your hands before you touch food.

lessons.title: Keep guests safe.
lessons.body: Know the way out. Keep walkways clear. Tell the organizer if a guest needs help you cannot give.
lessons.rule: A clear way out matters more than a tidy desk.
lessons.action: Walk the way out and move anything in the path.

lessons.title: Stay safe around power.
lessons.body: Do not touch bare wires. Keep water away from batteries and panels. Leave the work to someone trained if you are not sure.
lessons.rule: If you are not sure, do not touch it.
lessons.action: Stop and ask before you touch a wire.

lessons.title: Stay safe around water.
lessons.body: Keep the tank cover on. Do not drink from a tank that is not finished. Tell the organizer about a leak.
lessons.rule: A covered tank is safer than an open one.
lessons.action: Check that the tank cover is on.

lessons.title: Stay safe while you set up.
lessons.body: Use a steady ladder on firm ground. Do not climb in the rain or in strong wind. Ask someone to stand by while you climb.
lessons.rule: Stay on the ground when the weather is bad.
lessons.action: Check the ground under the ladder before you climb.

lessons.title: Keep the room safe.
lessons.body: Keep the way out clear. Know who to call if someone is hurt. Do not leave children alone in the room.
lessons.rule: Someone responsible stays in the room.
lessons.action: Check that the way out is clear.

lessons.title: Stay in your role.
lessons.body: Wash your hands. Do not give medicine. Call a trained person when someone is ill or hurt.
lessons.rule: Help with the room. Leave treatment to trained people.
lessons.action: Wash your hands and know who to call.

lessons.title: Take a photo of your work each day.
lessons.body: A photo shows what you did. It helps the organizer see the work. Take it in the daylight if you can.
lessons.rule: One photo a day is enough.
lessons.action: Take today's photo before you leave.

lessons.title: How your units grow.
lessons.body: Accepted work turns into ownership units. The organizer has to accept it first. How units pay out is not set yet. Do not expect a payout.
lessons.rule: Units are a record of your work, not cash in hand.
lessons.action: Log the work you did today.

lessons.title: Grow your work.
lessons.body: After you have done work on a project, you can start one of your own. You would be the organizer. You would find people and keep the records.
lessons.rule: Start only when you can look after it each week.
lessons.action: Start a project here.
